qs.q:
Match each message (1–5) and its meaning (A–F).
There is one letter that you do not need.

0. I haven't heard from you in ages. I was just wondering what was up with you. Is everything okay? [G = How are you?]
1. Don't forget to stop at the grocery. There's no point in having friends over if you have nothing to put in front of them.
2. I found an amazing cell phone online. My mum insists that I buy one in the local store. How can I convince her shopping on the Internet is perfectly safe?
3. My brother has just told me you called. I should've answered sooner. If you need me to come over, you should call me on my cell phone. My bad.
4. The school trip was great – except I lost my phone charger. My parents can't find out about it, or they'll ground me. Please, keep it a secret until I work something out!
5. As for the wedding party this Saturday, I know Mark is also invited. It's no secret you were just buying time avoiding each other. I'm sorry, but you two must make up before the big day.
items: 1 — Don't forget to stop at the grocery. Friends are coming over.
2 — Found amazing phone online. How can I convince mum the Internet is safe?
3 — I should've answered sooner. Call me on my cell phone. My bad.
4 — I lost my phone charger. Parents can't find out. Keep it secret!
5 — You and Mark must make up before the wedding this Saturday.

qs.q:
Why does Jack recommend visiting the Crown Jewels exhibition?

"When you get to London, I'd recommend the Tower of London and while you're there, don't miss the Crown Jewels exhibition. It'll be a nice change from all the military stuff and stories of former prisoners. I bought an excellent crown replica in their souvenir shop."

A To take a break from viewing weapons.
B To meet members of the Tower Guard.
C To buy jewellery.
opts: To take a break from viewing weapons.
To meet members of the Tower Guard.

What did Alex like about the music festival?

"What I found satisfying this time was how many bands were adding elements from other music styles. There was some trouble with the sound system during a few sets, though, which was quite disappointing considering the quality of music performed."

A The equipment was good quality.
B Most musicians played his favourite music style.
C Some groups experimented with different genres.
opts: Most musicians played his favourite music style.
Some groups experimented with different genres.

Why isn't Mia having the movie night as planned?

"I'm postponing our girls' movie night. My cousin Jake was voted Manager of the Year and won an all-expenses-paid city break. You know Stella has been dating him and he asked her to be his plus one. I told her we would wait."

A Because she is going away.
B Because her friend is going away.
C Because her cousin isn't going away.
opts: Because her friend is going away.
Because her cousin isn't going away.

Sitcoms

"Performed live, the full week was needed for technical details and for memorising scripts."

Why were the early sitcoms once-a-week programmes?
A Because each episode was about a single problem.
B Because the actors and crew needed time to prepare.
C Because viewers would otherwise miss some episodes.
opts: Because each episode was about a single problem.
Because the actors and crew needed time to prepare.
Because viewers would otherwise miss some episodes.

qs.q:
Sitcoms

"Since early cameras were quite large and difficult to move, the first sitcoms were shot on a single stage. 'The Honeymooners' was mostly set in a kitchen. At the kitchen table everyone had a place to gather and a reason to be there."

Why was the kitchen table used as the focus of the show in 'The Honeymooners'?
A Cameras were too big and couldn't be moved.
B That's where all the characters met over meals.
C It was a better option than the sofa in the living room.
opts: Cameras were too big and couldn't be moved.
That's where all the characters met over meals.
It was a better option than the sofa in the living room.

qs.q:
Sitcoms

"'I Love Lucy'... was the first to be filmed before live studio audiences and later included multiple sets. Even decades later popular shows like 'Three's Company' and 'The Cosby Show' didn't manage to match the number of sets 'Lucy' used in the 1950s."

Which sitcom was filmed on the largest number of sets?
A 'I Love Lucy'.
B 'The Cosby Show'.
C 'Three's Company'.

Sitcoms

"The 1970s sitcoms introduced REAL-WORLD EVENTS into their storylines, addressing social issues with humour. Studio audiences became the norm again."

How were the sitcoms of the 1970s different from those of the 1960s?
A They were about supernatural characters.
B They were not filmed in front of live audiences.
C They were about everyday problems and themes.
opts: They were not filmed in front of live audiences.
They were about everyday problems and themes.

qs.q:
Sitcoms

"Filmed programmes including 'Scrubs' and 'The Office' gained fame. Many of these shows used on-location filming, focusing on CAMERA WORK and EDITING, rather than scripted laughter, to improve the writing."

What characterises the programmes filmed in the 2000s?
A They used laugh tracks and scripted laughter.
B They were mostly filmed in front of studio audiences.
C They were made with more attention to technical details.
opts: They used laugh tracks and scripted laughter.
They were mostly filmed in front of studio audiences.
They were made with more attention to technical details.
